text:
melissa: Quick sync — I'm about to land a small Terraform change for Karpenter provisioners. Plan is: increase provisioner weight for batch-pool, reduce ttlSecondsUntilExpired from 30m -> 10m to reclaim idle spot nodes faster. Posting the diff for quick eyes before I merge.

melissa: TF snippet:```hcl
resource "karpenter_provisioner" "batch-pool" {
  name = "batch-pool"
  weight = 20 # was 10
  provider {
    instanceProfile = var.batch_instance_profile
    ttlSecondsUntilExpired = 600 # 10m
  }
}
```

melissa: Also tweaking labels so HPA targets can prefer on-demand fallback via nodeSelector: `k8s.redwood/capacity-type = on-demand` when spot unavailable.

aj: quick Q — why 10m? sounds aggressive for cold workloads. any risk of too much churn + increased launch rate?

melissa: good point. we see long idle tails on spot pools after batch jobs finish. most of the pods are short-lived (<5m). 10m should cut cost without too many launches. we can always raise to 15m after watching metrics.

sam: skimming the TF — did you update the kubelet eviction/taint tolerations? if we preempt spots a lot, pods might bounce onto on-demand and cause higher cost. also watch PDBs.

melissa: not touching kubelet evictions here. I added a toleration for `k8s.amazonaws.com/spot` in the batch chart so batch jobs can land on spot. PDBs for critical services untouched.

jeff: pinging for infra review: I can take a look. Can you also paste the Karpenter Provisioner CRD yaml you're planning to apply? need to check consolidation:```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: batch-pool
spec:
  consolidation: true
  ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 600
  provider:
    instanceProfile: "${var.batch_instance_profile}"
  labels:
    k8s.redwood/capacity-type: spot
  requirements:
    - key: karpenter.k8s.aws/capacity-type
      operator: In
      values: [spot, on-demand]
```

aj: also thoughts on Cluster Autoscaler? we're running CA on a few clusters in addition to Karpenter — need to make sure they don't fight.

melissa: CA is disabled on this cluster; we only had it for a migration path. I'll double check there's no helm release left.

sam: secret wiring note — if pods fall back to on-demand and use the same instance role, fine. but if we use node-level IAM via instance profile, make sure service-account-iam is configured for the kube2iam / IRSA mapping. otherwise some jobs need KMS access might fail.

melissa: thanks — infra side already has IRSA for the batch SA. I'm adding a comment in the PR to verify the role mapping: `iam.amazonaws.com/role: batch-exec-role`.

jeff: LGTM for the TF changes, one nit: bumping weight is fine but could starve other provisioning patterns if you rely on custom weighting across multiple provisioners. watch the scheduler logs. :eyes:

melissa: noted. will watch `karpenter-controller` metrics + `provisioning_latency` dashboards after deploy.

infra-bot: terraform plan finished — no drift detected, 3 resources to be changed. (run: #1234) :white_check_mark:

melissa: thanks infra-bot. I'll merge in 15m unless anyone objects.

aj: would appreciate a heads up when merged so I can add a ticket to watch cost/scale metrics for the next 48h.

melissa: will do. merging in ~10. :thumbsup:

jeff: quick follow-up after merge — if we see higher churn we should consider increasing `ttlSecondsUntilExpired` to 15m and enable `consolidation.provisioner` stabilization windows.

melissa: adding that to the follow-up checklist.

sam: cheers — thanks for the PR ping, melissa.

melissa: thanks all!
